exodus.16.p1.b1.text: On the fifteenth day of the second month after they had left the land of Egypt, the whole congregation of Israel set out from Elim and came to the Desert of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai.

exodus.16.p1.b2.text: If only we had died by the LORD’s hand in the land of Egypt!

exodus.16.p1.b3.text: There we sat by pots of meat and ate our fill of bread,

exodus.16.p1.b4.text: but you have brought us into this desert to starve this whole assembly to death!

exodus.16.p2.b5.text: Behold, I will rain down bread from heaven for you. Each day the people are to go out and gather enough for that day. In this way I will test whether or not they will follow My instructions.

exodus.16.p2.b6.text: This evening you will know that it was the LORD who brought you out of the land of Egypt,

exodus.16.p2.b7.text: Who are we? Your grumblings are not against us but against the LORD.

exodus.16.p3.b8.text: Tell the whole congregation of Israel, ‘Come before the LORD, for He has heard your grumbling.’

exodus.16.p3.b9.text: And as Aaron was speaking to the whole congregation of Israel, they looked toward the desert, and there in a cloud the glory of the LORD appeared.

exodus.16.p3.b10.text: Tell them, ‘At twilight you will eat meat, and in the morning you will be filled with bread. Then you will know that I am the LORD your God.’

exodus.16.p4.b11.text: That evening quail came and covered the camp,

exodus.16.p4.b12.text: When the layer of dew had evaporated, there were thin flakes on the desert floor, as fine as frost on the ground.

exodus.16.p4.b14.text: It is the bread that the LORD has given you to eat.

exodus.16.p5.b15.text: So the Israelites did this. Some gathered more, and some less.

exodus.16.p5.b16.text: When they measured it by the omer, he who gathered much had no excess, and he who gathered little had no shortfall.

exodus.16.p5.b17.text: No one may keep any of it until morning.

exodus.16.p5.b18.text: some people left part of it until morning, and it became infested with maggots and began to smell. So Moses was angry with them.

exodus.16.p6.b19.text: On the sixth day, they gathered twice as much food—two omers per person

exodus.16.p6.b20.text: This is what the LORD has said: ‘Tomorrow is to be a day of complete rest, a holy Sabbath to the LORD. So bake what you want to bake, and boil what you want to boil. Then set aside whatever remains and keep it until morning.’

exodus.16.p6.b21.text: So they set it aside until morning as Moses had commanded, and it did not smell or contain any maggots.

exodus.16.p6.b22.text: For six days you may gather, but on the seventh day, the Sabbath, it will not be there.”

exodus.16.p7.b23.text: Yet on the seventh day some of the people went out to gather, but they did not find anything.

exodus.16.p7.b24.text: How long will you refuse to keep My commandments and instructions?

exodus.16.p7.b25.text: So the people rested on the seventh day.

exodus.16.p8.b26.text: Now the house of Israel called the bread manna. It was white like coriander seed and tasted like wafers made with honey.

exodus.16.p8.b27.text: Take a jar and fill it with an omer of manna. Then place it before the LORD to be preserved for the generations to come.

exodus.16.p8.b28.text: to be preserved just as the LORD had commanded Moses…

exodus.16.p8.b29.text: The Israelites ate manna forty years, until they came to a land where they could settle; they ate manna until they reached the border of Canaan.
